newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea orders arrest of student leaders.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea orders arrest of student leaders.

text.p: South Korea's chief prosecutor ordered prosecution officials to seek out and "severely punish" those responsible for the death of a riot police officer during clashes with militant students on Monday.

A proescution statement quoted Kim Ki-Soo as saying that he had called on authorities around the country to search for the top leaders of an outlawed left-wing student body which has orchestrated four days of violent protests in Seoul to demand the resignation of President Kim Young-sam.
The statement said Kim "ordered Seoul prosecutors to quickly detain the criminals involved in the death of policeman Yoo Ji-woong."

He said he had ordered prosecution officials nation-wide to seek out the main leaders of the Hanchongryon who have led the violence in Seoul by throwing fire bombs and wielding steel pipes. The government says the outlawed body takes orders from North Korea and is a threat to national security.
Kim was quoted as saying the protests were "a violent uprising" that had disrupted the capital by stopping trains.
The violence was sparked by the president's refusal to bow to opposition demands and reveal how much he spent on his 1992 election campaign.
